title: Portals, refs and reaching the DOM when you have to

videos.script:
Most of React is description: you say what the page looks like, and React makes it so. A few things the browser will only do when asked. Today is about asking.

{{dom}} First, when describing is not enough: focus, a modal dialog, scrolling, measuring. Each needs the element itself, and a ref is how you get it.

{{dialog}} Then the browser's own dialog. A ref, an effect that calls showModal, and the close event coming back. You will see what the browser does for free: focus goes in, Escape closes, focus comes back.

{{field}} Then a field component that passes its ref on. In React nineteen a ref is just a prop, and the form library needs it to reach the input.

{{portal}} And last, a portal: a message that React renders from the course screen and the browser finds under the body. Why it goes there, why it is always rendered, and when you do not need one at all.
